conventions.deferred:: A real obligation this plan carries later; the suffix names the milestone. Used for pictures whose content is normative but whose milestone has not run: the picture is reviewed now so that its exclusion or its deferral is a decision, and the disposition moves to a `formalized:` declaration when the milestone lands.
conventions.formalized:: A Lean declaration path that carries this picture's meaning (the same commitment form as for clauses).
conventions.informative: The picture illustrates clauses that are formalized elsewhere, and adds no obligation of its own.
conventions.test:: A vector id whose expectation is the picture's observable form: the worked examples carry exact octets, so the vectors that replay them are the witness, and every id recorded here is resolved against vectors/** by the same gate that resolves a clause's.

amqp-core-security-v1.0-os.xml#picture.5.note: The SASL Frame: its type code, the octets the channel field occupies and that they carry no meaning, the recommendation that DOFF be two, the size bound and the requirement that the body hold exactly one AMQP type providing `sasl-frame`. The frame shape is already formalized (S2's SASL frame type and the descriptor-role check); what remains is the mechanism negotiation and the layer-transition rules, which are S7's. **Carried this session, and the reporter's own words for it**: formalized:Spec.Frame.channelOctets; formalized:Spec.Frame.saslTypeCode; formalized:Spec.Frame.carriesPerformative; formalized:Spec.Frame.readFrame; formalized:Spec.Connection.stepSaslFrame; formalized:Spec.Connection.bodylessFrame

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#picture..clause_text: Frame Connection Session Link ======================================== open H begin I H attach I H flow I H transfer I H disposition I H detach I H end I H c...
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#picture..note: The Frame Dispatch Table: which endpoint handles which performative (open and close at the connection, begin/attach/flow/transfer/disposition/detach/end intercepted at the connection and handled at the session). It is the dispatch dimension of the slice and has no clause behind it.

The Protocol Header Layout: four octets of "AMQP", a protocol id octet, then major, minor and revision. The section states the exchange in prose and the mandated error conditions nowhere, so this layout is the header's definition. S3 formalizes it as the negotiation's first four fields; the version-mismatch condition is an ambiguity recorded in the register.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#picture..clause_text: [picture] Frame Layout: REQUIRED OPTIONAL OPTIONAL +--------------+-----------------+------------+ | frame header | extended header | frame body | +--------------+-----------------+...
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#picture..note: The frame layout is the structure: `Frame` carries the extended header's octets separately from the body (lean/Spec/Frame.lean:193-213), `headerOctets`, `sizeOctets`, `doffOctets` and `channelOctets` (lean/Spec/Frame.lean:86-108) are the fixed widths, and `bodyStart doff = doff * 4` (lean/Spec/Frame.lean:216) is the arithmetic that places the body after the extended header. The REQUIRED/OPTIONAL distinction the picture draws is the one the framing clauses state in prose — the header is required, the extended header and body are optional.

The general frame layout: SIZE, DOFF, TYPE, the type-specific remainder of the header, and the extended header and body widths as the differences DOFF and SIZE imply. Formalized by the frame structure plus `bodyStart` and the two proved arithmetic theorems, which is why the extended header's width is a theorem rather than a comment.

The AMQP frame layout: the fixed eight-octet header whose fields are SIZE, DOFF, TYPE and CHANNEL (lean/Spec/Frame.lean:86-108), then the body at `bodyStart doff` (lean/Spec/Frame.lean:216). The TYPE octet is read against the generated table — `FrameType.code` and `FrameType.ofCode` (lean/Spec/Frame.lean:127-136) — so the picture's frame type 0x00 comes from the table rather than from a literal here, and the two CHANNEL octets are kept rather than interpreted (lean/Spec/Frame.lean:193-213).

The Connection State Diagram: the same machine as picture.24 drawn as transitions, and its value is the transitions rather than the states — which is why both are dispositioned rather than one being called a duplicate of the other.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#picture..clause_text: State Legal Sends Legal Receives Legal Connection Actions ======================================================================= START HDR HDR HDR_RCVD HDR ...
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#picture..note: The Connection State Table: fourteen states with the frames each permits and the connection action each implies. It is the only normative statement of the connection lifecycle anywhere in the artifacts — the section has clauses for individual rules (channel zero, close ordering, idle timeouts) and no clause for the state dimension itself — so it is not a diagram to be summarised but the machine's source. S3 formalizes it as the state type and its transition relation, and this disposition moves to a `formalized:` path then.

The session state machine's only statement in the artifact: the states are `atState`'s branches, the transitions are the `Session.after*` family (`afterBegin`, `afterEnd` among them), and its ten edges are the model the session sweep was built from and the machine both artefacts implement. Disposed although the text scan flags it `looks_normative: false`, because that scan keys on grammar and normative keywords and a graph has neither: the diagram's content is structural, which is the one class the flag cannot see. Recorded here so the exclusion is a decision rather than an artifact of the flag.

The outgoing fragmentation state diagram: when a transfer may carry more, and what the sender must do at each point. Fragmentation is S4's scope, and this is its source. **Carried this session, and the reporter's own words for it**: formalized:Spec.Session.transferLink. The outgoing fragmentation state machine: NOT_SENT/SENDING/SENT/ABORTED are delivery=none / delivery.isSome / cleared-on-completion / cleared-on-abort, which is exactly what transferLink computes, and vectors/flow.ndjson (34 vectors, all 29 interior split points) is the pin. Vacuous part: the diagram draws no NOT_SENT --A=1--> ABORTED arrow, which the model admits (a first transfer that aborts); that is a diagram gap, not a model gap.

The incoming fragmentation state diagram: the receiver's counterpart of picture.57, and the reason both exist — one side's obligation is not the other's. **Carried this session, and the reporter's own words for it**: formalized:Spec.Session.transferLink. The receiver's counterpart, the same function in the receiving direction; the flow corpus is all receive steps, so it is the direction that corpus exercises.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.1.clause_text: [picture] Primitive Format Code (String): constructor untyped bytes | | +--+ +-----------------+-----------------+ | | | | ... 0xA1 0x1E "Hello Glorious Messaging World" ... | | | | | | | | utf8 byte...
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.1.note: Worked example of the str8-utf8 encoding: 0xA1 0x1E followed by 30 octets, every byte exact. The writer is `writeVariableData` (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:771-785) — a size field of the subcategory width, then that many octets — and the reader's half is `readVariable` (`.7`); the three vectors pin the encoded octets, the round trip, and the refusal of a string whose octets run short. The two vector ids this note used to name (`str8-hello`, `described-url`) were never in the corpus, which no gate could see because a note's citations are resolved only when the note names a corpus file — they are recorded as `test:` values now, where the vector gate resolves them.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.18.clause_text:
[picture] Example Composite Type:

An example composite type.
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.18.note: Worked example of a composite type definition: the book type in descriptor domain 0x00000003 with field multiplicities and a mandatory title. The declared fields come from the generated table through `fieldDeclsOf` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:278-284) and the rules a body must meet — mandatory present, no longer than the declaration, types as declared — are `checkFieldList` (lean/Spec/Message.lean:491-522), which is what makes this figure the model for how a described list maps onto declared fields.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.19.clause_text: [picture] Example Composite Value: constructor list representation of a book | | +-----------------+-------------------+ +-------------+---------------+ | | | | 0x00 0xA3 0x11 "example:book:li...
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.19.note: Worked example of a composite value, and the reference for the size field's scope: its list8 size 0x40 counts the count octet, the title, the authors array (39 octets on the wire) and the null isbn. That arithmetic is `readCompound`'s check (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:448-480), and the three vectors pin the decode, the encode and the refusal of a size that disagrees with the octets measured.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.2.clause_text: [picture] Described Format Code (URL): constructor untyped bytes | | +-----------+-----------+ +-----------------+-----------------+ | | | | ... 0x00 0xA1 0x03 "URL" 0xA1 0x1E "http://example.org/...
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.2.note: Worked example of a described value: 0x00, a descriptor, then the value. That is `readValue`'s descriptor branch (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:425-435), which reads a value, then a value, and returns the pair as a described value; the picture's own claim — that a string-typed descriptor is reserved, which is why symbolic descriptors are the modelled case — is a statement about the artifact's descriptor domain rather than a rule this layer enforces, and the two vectors pin the described example in both directions.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.3.clause_text: [picture] Constructor BNF: constructor = format-code / %x00 descriptor constructor format-code = fixed / variable / compound / array fixed = empty / fixed-one / fixed-two / fixed-four ...
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.3.note: Normative: this is the formal constructor grammar — the format-code ranges, the %x00 descriptor prefix, and the reserved octets. It is the specification's own normative statement of which octets are format codes, so the codec's accepted set is checked against these ranges as a theorem rather than asserted.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.4.note: Layout: a constructor followed by untyped bytes, with the constructor stating how to read them. This is the picture behind the classification function.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.5.clause_text: [picture] Subcategory Formats: Subcategory Category Format ============================================================================== 0x4 Fixed Width Zero octets of data. 0x5 Fixed Wid...
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.5.note: The subcategory table: 0x4/0x5/0x6/0x7/0x8/0x9 are fixed widths of 0/1/2/4/8/16 octets, 0xA/0xB variable with one or four size octets, 0xC/0xD compound with one or four size and count octets, 0xE/0xF array with one or four size and count octets. The widths are the `width` each `Constructor` carries (lean/Spec/Value.lean:40-55) as `classify` assigns it (lean/Spec/Value.lean:56-70), and the generated corpus exercises them: the ubyte/byte/ushort family in vectors/generated.ndjson and the uint vectors in vectors/primitives.ndjson all cite this picture.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.6.clause_text: [picture] Layout of Fixed Width Data Encodings: n OCTETs +----------+ | data | +----------+ Subcategory n ================= 0x4 0 0x5 1 0x6 2 0x7 4 0x8 8 0x9 16
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.6.note: Layout of fixed-width encodings: the constructor determines the data size, with no length field. `readFixed` (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:347-383) reads a value of the declared width and consumes nothing else, which is the sentence as code.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.7.clause_text: [picture] Layout of Variable Width Data Encodings: n OCTETs size OCTETs +----------+-------------+ | size | value | +----------+-------------+ Subcategory n ================= 0xA 1 0xB 4
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.7.note: Layout of variable-width encodings: a size field of the subcategory width, then that many octets. `readVariable` (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:384-397) reads the size at the declared width and then that many octets, and the width itself is `classify`'s (`.5`).

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.8.clause_text: [picture] Layout of Compound Data Encodings: +----------= count items =----------+ | | n OCTETs n OCTETs | | +----------+----------+--------------+------------+-------+ | size | count | ... /| item |\ ....
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.8.note: Layout of compound encodings: size, count, then count constructed items. `readCompound` (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:448-480) reads the size, then the count, then the items, and checks the size against the octets it measured; the scope of the size field is decided in ledger/ambiguities/compound-size-field.json, which this picture is the source for.

amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.9.clause_text: [picture] Layout of Array Encodings: +--= count elements =--+ | | n OCTETs n OCTETs | | +----------+----------+---------------------+-------+------+-------+ | size | count | element-constructor ...
amqp-core-types-v1.0-os.xml#picture.9.note: Layout of array encodings: size, count, one element constructor, then the elements in that constructor's form. `readArrayData` (lean/Spec/Codec.lean:481-498) reads exactly that, checks the declared size against the octets measured, and bounds the count by `arrayElementLimit` because a zero-width element constructor leaves the count bounded by nothing in the data; this figure is the arithmetic check that fixes the size field's scope.

scope: Pictures whose content is normative rather than illustrative. Every picture is listed in ledger/pictures.json; those containing formal grammar or normative keywords are flagged reviewable and must carry a decision, so excluding a subtree is an explicit act rather than a default.
